decisions.point: JWT verification library for CF Access
decisions.chosen: jose (Workers-compatible, ESM, used by Cloudflare's own examples)
alternatives: Hand-rolled WebCrypto RS256 + manual JWKS parsing
decisions.rationale: jose is the smallest Workers-compatible jwt+JWKS lib, supports remote JWKS with caching, and avoids the high-risk hand-roll of RS256 signature verification. jsonwebtoken depends on Node crypto and won't run in the Worker runtime.

decisions.point: HTML sanitizer for editor html-block output
decisions.chosen: Hand-rolled regex allowlist (tags, attrs, URL schemes) sized to legacy parity
decisions.rationale: Workers runtime has no DOM. dompurify needs jsdom (huge + not edge-friendly). The legacy code uses a regex allowlist; we replicate that pattern with explicit tests asserting <script>, on* attributes, and javascript: URLs are stripped.

alternatives: Full JWT signed with jose (extra dep coupling, larger payload)
Random URL-only signed token + KV lookup (extra KV write per preview)
decisions.rationale: Preview tokens are short-lived and never leave the surface; HMAC keeps the signing path one Web Crypto call without depending on jose. Avoids KV round-trip for ephemeral previews.

decisions.point: AI endpoint behavior when OPENAI_API_KEY unset
decisions.chosen: Return 501 Not Implemented with explanatory JSON body
alternatives: Return 200 with mock body (encourages downstream to wire real calls prematurely)
Return 200 + always call OpenAI (Phase 1 explicitly defers AI provisioning)
decisions.rationale: User spec line 104 prohibits calling OpenAI in Phase 1 unless OPENAI_API_KEY exists. 501 is the honest signal; mock 200 hides the wiring gap and risks downstream consumers caching fake responses.

decisions.chosen: Return 404 unless slug matches a published page row; reserved paths short-circuit to 404 before this lookup
alternatives: Always render-as-page (ambiguous: every URL becomes a page)
301 redirect to /page/:slug (breaks legacy bookmarks for content not yet ported)
decisions.rationale: The legacy compatibility surface is a placeholder; 404 for non-pages is the safe default. Reserved-path guard MUST run first to keep /admin etc. from leaking into this lookup.

decisions.chosen: Add legacy team-domain (kodigital2.cloudflareaccess.com), legacy admin host (admin.theiwise.com), legacy CF_ACCESS_AUD hex, legacy D1 id, legacy KV id; do NOT add the shared account_id a05d7505b71c6cd931e436defe670509
alternatives: Tighten only legacy hostname (insufficient — IDs leak through copied code)
Add account_id a05d7505b71c6cd931e436defe670509 to denylist (would break this Worker — shared account)
decisions.rationale: Shared account_id is allow-listed by orchestrator instructions; banning it would break the new Worker's own deploy. Other 5 identifiers are legacy-only and would create cross-tenant config leak if copied.

decisions.chosen: Thin parameterized prepare/bind wrappers, no ORM
alternatives: Full SQL builder (e.g. drizzle, kysely) — Workers compat varies, increases bundle size
Inline prepare/bind at every call site — repeats ?? defaults and JSON.parse safety patterns
decisions.rationale: Wrappers centralize the workspace D1 safety rules (?? for numeric defaults, parameterized only, JSON.parse wrapped with try/catch + cache-miss recovery) without the Workers-bundle cost of an ORM.

Run npm install + npm run typecheck + npm test + npm run verify:no-legacy-prod-refs
Smoke-test wrangler dev: GET /health 200, GET /admin 401, GET /api/privacy/status 200

risk_controls: No production data migration this phase (mission_draft.risk.production_data_risk=false)
AI endpoints return 501 by default — no accidental OpenAI cost
DEV_BYPASS_AUTH only honored when APP_ENV=development AND env truthy (double gate)
site_id columns deferred to Phase 2 — only TODO markers in 0001_init_cms.sql
All D1 calls parameterized via prepare(...).bind(...) — verify by AC T2.AC1 (zero matches for ${} interpolation)
JWKS cache TTL fixed at 86400s — verify by AC T3.AC2
verify:no-legacy-prod-refs run as final gate before push (AC T13.AC2)
rollback_plan: Revert merge commit of mission/kodigital-homepages-cms-phase1-2026-05-09 on main (single squash commit). Phase 1 introduces no production data; KV CACHE namespace can be cleared via Dashboard if stale; if 0001_init_cms.sql was applied to remote D1, run `npx wrangler d1 execute kodigital-homepages-cms-db --remote --command 'DROP TABLE IF EXISTS articles; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS article_versions; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS categories; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS tags; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS article_tags; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS pages; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS media; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS redirects; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS site_settings; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS prompt_presets; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS privacy_opt_outs;'` (safe — Phase 1 carries no tenant data). R2 MEDIA bucket retains uploaded objects; can be purged separately if needed.
evidence_plan: vitest exit code per test file (test_exit_code parser)
grep counts per AC (parse_grep_count parser) for surface declarations and denylist additions
wrangler dev curl smoke against /health, /admin, /api/privacy/status (parse_curl_response parser via captured output)
call_path_expectation: Phase 1 introduces no cross-service calls. All routes resolve within the Worker. CF Access JWT validates via JWKS fetched from CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN, cached in KV CACHE for 24h. R2 MEDIA serves blobs directly. D1 reads/writes go through api/src/db/index.ts wrappers. Preview HMAC verification is in-process via Web Crypto.

implementation_route.justification: Multi-module port with schema mutation across 13 stories spanning auth/editor/workflow/media/privacy/admin/public/preview. One Ralph cycle plus Evaluator review; max 2 fix cycles before escalation.
